topology: PC1 and PC2 reach R1 TCP 830 through separate routed management LANs. R1 Gi0/1 carries SRV1 data traffic; Loopback10 is created through real NETCONF RPCs.
implemented: Offline browser NETCONF client under PC Desktop / Network tools: actual TCP 830 and logical SSH authentication, hello capabilities, session/message IDs, editable RPC examples, retained bounded transcript and JSON download.
Local AAA with privilege-15 operator and rejected privilege-1 observer; authentication passwords are cleared from the form and excluded from protocol transcripts and observation history.
Filtered get-config configuration versus get operational state and counters; running edit creates Loopback10 and its real local route; fresh delivered ICMP replies prove reachability.
Invalid multi-interface edit rejects bad IPv4 data atomically without shutting the data interface or creating the invalid loopback.
IOS XE candidate transition resets existing sessions, removes writable-running, advertises candidate and confirmed-commit 1.0, and rejects running edits in candidate mode.
Independent client sessions exercise candidate lock conflict, isolated edits, actual candidate reads, discard and commit.

Unconfirmed data-interface shutdown interrupts actual forwarding; simulation-clock rollback restores it while the separate management session remains open. A second confirmed commit is explicitly confirmed and survives its deadline.
Temporary ingress ACL blocks only PC1 TCP 830, preserves PC1 ICMP and PC2 management, and requires a successful PC1 read after ACL removal.
Unlock, close-session, startup save, correct final addressing, no pending candidate/confirmation/locks and zero active sessions are verified.

Runtime-only bounded 128-record server history and 100-message client transcript are correlated by actual channel/message IDs and delivered replies; completed observations persist through YAML while runtime is discarded.
Practice begins at 0/20; completed reference has six live configuration tasks only, no pre-earned RPC or traffic observations; missing imported teaching interfaces fail closed.
scope: IOS XE teaching subset: NETCONF base 1.0 end-of-message framing, modeled SSH, bounded ietf-interfaces/ietf-ip and native hostname data.
No claim of real SSH cryptography, NETCONF 1.1 chunk framing, full YANG library, subscriptions, startup/copy-config RPCs, or confirmed-commit 1.1 persistence/cancel-commit.
Primary Cisco documentation and RFC 6241 reviewed. No new live CML capture was performed.
Terminal styling, node artwork and existing UI theme are unchanged.
